title: Temperature is what a thermometer reads, not a store of heat
summary: Temperature is what a thermometer measures. It tells how hot or cold something is, and it is not itself a store of heat.
body: OpenStax Physics says temperature is defined by the instrument used to tell how hot or cold an object is, on a scale people invented. The page's words are that temperature is literally defined as what we measure on a thermometer. The same section warns that temperature is not a measure of heat. Heat is energy moving because of a temperature difference, which is a different card. Three common scales are named: Fahrenheit, Celsius, and kelvin. How those scales are anchored, and the kelvin definition, sit on the linked cards. This card is the thermometer definition only.
